intent: You can get a mechanical keyboard for 40 dollars now, while the boards enthusiasts rave about run 150 to 200, sometimes listing the very same switch names. I type maybe six hours a day and I'm tempted by the cheap one, but I don't want to buy twice. Where does the extra money actually go, in things like the case, plate, stabilizers, build, and does any of it change day-to-day typing rather than sound in close-up videos? Is there a price above which I'm paying for hobby cachet, and which board sits right at that cutoff?

intent_v1_legacy: I've been lurking in FIRE communities for a year and I can't tell the gospel from the fantasy anymore. People confidently claim $1M at 45 works fine on the 4% rule, that moving to Thailand or Mexico slashes costs 70%, that house-hacking beats index funds to early retirement, that healthcare is the real killer before Medicare, and that Bogleheads overhype sequence-of-returns risk. Which of these actually survive scrutiny? I especially want the real story on sequence risk, since my whole plan hinges on it. A blunt reality-check list at the end would be perfect.
